PHEIC CONTEXT: WHO declared mpox a Public Health Emergency of International Concern (PHEIC) on 14 August 2024, driven substantially by the DRC clade Ib outbreak — expect elevated reporting volume, potential data revisions, and multiple overlapping sitreps during this window

CLADE SPECIFICITY: DRC August 2024 data involves both endemic clade I and the newly characterized clade Ib (associated with sexual transmission networks in eastern DRC, particularly South Kivu) — distinguish clade when reported
DATA COMPLETENESS: DRC surveillance infrastructure is resource-constrained; significant underreporting is expected, especially at health-zone and community levels
LANGUAGE: Primary official DRC sources are in French — query terms and source reading must accommodate French-language content ('cas', 'décès', 'flambée', 'bulletin épidémiologique', etc.)
TEMPORAL OVERLAP: August 2024 data may appear in reports dated September or October 2024 (retrospective sitreps) — do not restrict source search strictly to August publication dates

EXTRACTION MODEL WARNING (from task_input_warnings): extraction_record_model_still_hantavirus_named — verify that the extraction schema in use has been updated to Mpox-appropriate field names before ingestion; do not allow Hantavirus-specific fields to contaminate Mpox records

SOURCE DISCOVERY WARNING (from task_input_warnings): source_discovery_not_yet_disease_generic — source discovery pipeline may not yet be fully generalized; manually verify that Mpox-specific source categories (WHO DON, Africa CDC, INRB, DRC MoH) are included in the discovery scope
DOUBLE-COUNTING RISK: WHO, Africa CDC, and DRC MoH may report the same underlying data — cross-reference source chains and avoid double-counting when aggregating
SUBNATIONAL GRANULARITY: Prioritize province-level and health-zone-level data; national aggregates alone are insufficient for this collection task
EVIDENCE QUOTE REQUIREMENT: Every extracted record must include a verbatim evidence_quote from the source document supporting the numeric values recorded

iterative_source_discovery_summary.final_coverage_assessment: Iteration 1 surfaced strong candidate sources across international organizations (WHO, UNICEF, ECDC, CDC) and one INRB/ReliefWeb French-language sitrep. The UNICEF SitRep (20 Aug–1 Sep 2024) snippet contains a partial aggregate figure (20,015 suspected cases, 632 deaths as of week 35) but this is a year-to-date cumulative figure, not an August-only monthly total. The ReliefWeb sitrep No. 025 (29 Aug 2024) is the most directly relevant national source but only appeared as a title/URL — no numeric content was confirmed. WHO DON 2024-DON522 covers the DRC outbreak context but its snippet does not contain August 2024 case counts. The PMC article on Kokolo health zone (Kinshasa) covers August–November 2024 and could provide locality-level data. Africa CDC was not represented in the top results despite being a primary source for weekly African Mpox data. WHO AFRO external situation reports for August 2024 (sitrep nos. covering epi weeks 31–35) were not directly surfaced. Coverage is promising but incomplete for the target fields.
iterative_source_discovery_summary.final_trustworthiness_assessment: High-trust sources identified: WHO DON (who.int), UNICEF SitRep (unicef.org), ReliefWeb-hosted DRC sitrep No. 025 (reliefweb.int, sourced from DRC Ministry of Health/INRB), ECDC (ecdc.europa.eu), INRB (inrb.cd), CDC HAN (cdc.gov), PMC peer-reviewed article (pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov). Medium-trust: MSF/Doctors Without Borders (operational context, not primary surveillance data), NETEC (secondary summary). Low-trust: facebook.com posts (not usable as primary evidence). The facebook.com results should be excluded from evidence extraction. The ReliefWeb sitrep No. 025 and INRB result are the highest-priority targets for August 2024 subnational data.
